evals.prompt: hi, I'm the ops lead for our UK road freight team. customers keep ringing the service desk asking "where's my delivery" when a truck is running late - it's like 30% of our calls some weeks. I want the system to automatically email the customer when a delivery is going to be late. can you write this up as a spec I can hand to the dev team? I'm in meetings all afternoon so just draft it and flag whatever you need from me.
evals.expected_output:
A Markdown spec file for proactive late-delivery emails, written without any codebase. It separates
confirmed facts from stated facts and assumptions, does not invent system internals as facts, puts
technical unknowns as questions for engineering, has testable Given/When/Then acceptance criteria,
explicit decisions with recommendations (e.g. what counts as "late"), edge cases, out of scope,
rollout/undo, and success measures tied to the 30% call volume.
assertions: A Markdown spec file is saved
The spec has numbered acceptance criteria written in Given/When/Then form
Every acceptance criterion names the gap or requirement it covers
Statements about the current situation are each explicitly labelled as confirmed, stated by someone, or an assumption
The spec has a decisions section in which each decision has a recommendation and a named decider/owner
The spec defines 'late' with a concrete numeric threshold
The spec has an out-of-scope section
The spec states how to switch the feature off / undo it
The spec has a success measure that uses the ~30% call share as a baseline and sets a target

evals.prompt: I'm the product owner for our internal HR tools. Managers keep complaining that at month end they have to approve leave requests one by one - some have 40 direct reports. I'd like a spec for letting managers approve leave requests in bulk, so I can hand it to our two developers. The app's code is in the leave-app folder. I won't be able to answer questions until tomorrow, so go ahead and draft it.
evals.expected_output:
A Markdown spec for manager bulk approval that is grounded in the leave-app code: it cites files
(and ideally lines), discovers the existing HR-admin bulk_approve in admin.py and that it skips the
audit log, balance check, direct-report check and emails (breaking README rules), applies the four
README rules to the new design, handles partial failure (some requests fail balance), email volume
vs the 60/minute SMTP limit, and has testable acceptance criteria and decisions.
assertions: A Markdown spec file is saved
The spec identifies the existing HR-admin bulk_approve endpoint in admin.py
The spec states that the existing bulk_approve skips the audit log (README rule 1)
The spec cites code locations with file and line numbers (e.g. routes.py:NN)
The spec defines behaviour when some requests in a batch fail (partial failure)
The spec addresses the 60 emails/minute SMTP limit from notify.py
The spec has numbered acceptance criteria written in Given/When/Then form
Every acceptance criterion names the gap or requirement it covers
The spec has a decisions section in which each decision has a recommendation and a named decider/owner

evals.prompt: Our BA wrote the attached spec for invoice downloads in the customer portal. Engineering wants to start on it next sprint. Can you review it and tell me if it's ready to go? Please save your review as a file too.
evals.expected_output:
A saved review of the invoice spec with a clear verdict (not ready), item-by-item findings with
quotes from the spec as evidence: no testable acceptance criteria, vague terms ("fast",
"user-friendly", "last invoices"), unverified assumptions stated as facts (SAP PDFs in SharePoint;
finance no longer handling emails), no out of scope, no decisions, missing edge cases (multi-account
users, credit notes, missing PDFs), and access-control/personal-data questions. Offers a retrofit
rather than silently rewriting.
assertions: A review file is saved and the input spec is unchanged
The review gives an explicit verdict that the spec is not ready
The review flags the contradiction between linking SharePoint PDFs and fetching from the SAP API
The review flags vague, untestable wording such as 'fast' and 'user-friendly'
The review flags the absence of acceptance criteria
The review scores the spec item by item against named criteria, quoting the spec as evidence
The review flags 'Finance will no longer need to handle invoice emails' as an outcome/assumption rather than a buildable requirement
The review proposes default answers or a retrofit for the open decisions rather than only listing problems
